source_review.notes: Checked current official Apache Spark RDD, cluster, and scheduling documentation; Apache Beam model, runtime, and runner documentation; Apache Flink ExecutionPlan and JobGraph APIs; Dask task and high-level graph documentation; and the original Dryad and MapReduce publications. All twelve URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date. Sources support DAG representation, logical-to-physical execution, stages/tasks, scheduling, exchanges, runner variation, graph optimization, and lineage/recovery claims.

evidence: Reviewed finite DAG G=(V,E), predecessor and successor sets, indegree/outdegree, paths, cycles, topological order, edge kinds, stages, task attempts, and artifact contracts.
Reviewed vertex duration d(v), earliest finish EF(v), total work W, span S, modeled capacity P, and resource/work lower bounds.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Logical vertices, physical operators, partition tasks, attempts, stages, edge artifacts, and committed outputs remain explicitly distinct.

evidence: Executed dag-stage-and-critical-path with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced seven vertices in deterministic lexical topological order.
Recomputed stage 0 as the two read/parse branches, stage 1 as join, and stage 2 as aggregate plus narrow publish.
Recomputed earliest finishes and the read_b, parse_b, join, aggregate, publish critical path at 18 duration units; confirmed a two-node cycle is rejected.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Eighteen is correctly labeled as a structural lower bound under unlimited resources and zero unmodeled overhead, not a production duration prediction.

evidence: Checked Kahn traversal removes zero-indegree vertices, decrements child indegrees, emits all vertices exactly for a DAG, and detects a residual directed cycle otherwise.
Verified EF(v)=d(v)+max predecessor EF with zero for roots and checked the maximum earliest finish identifies the modeled critical path.
Reviewed abstract stage assignment as maximum predecessor stage plus one across exchange edges and zero across narrow edges.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The stage recurrence is presented as an abstract model and does not claim to encode every engine barrier, broadcast, reuse, or operator-capability rule.

evidence: Reviewed empty graphs, multiple sources and sinks, self-edges, missing dependency closure, multiple valid topological orders, cycles, bounded unrolling, hidden external feedback, and million-task graph overhead.

Reviewed fan-in blockage, fan-out lifetime, exchange skew, high-cardinality partitions, incompatible fusion resources, cache eviction, nondeterministic recomputation, and long-lineage recovery amplification.

Reviewed failed/speculative attempts, ambiguous timeouts, partial publication, non-idempotent database/payment/notification effects, cancellation, stale policy, cross-region placement, and sensitive lineage.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Static acyclicity, edge readiness, resource feasibility, runtime deadlock freedom, semantic equivalence, and effect safety are separate obligations.

evidence: Traced graph and plan digests, code/configuration, schemas, partitioning, input and side-input snapshots, security context, tasks/attempts, artifact digests, and commit winners.
Checked consumers use only edge-valid authoritative outputs and retries isolate candidates until commit.
Checked physical rewrites preserve logical observable semantics while exchanges, barriers, caches, and external effects retain explicit contracts.
invariant_checking.notes: Readiness requires dependency contract satisfaction plus resource, placement, data, identity, and policy admission where applicable.

evidence: Reviewed the twelve-step audit from selected sinks and vertex/edge contracts through cycle proof, physical rewrites, stages/tasks, lower bounds, materialization, retry/commit, and replay.

Checked counterexamples for source-order execution, arbitrary readiness, vertex-equals-task, display-layer stages, universal fusion/cache benefits, lineage-based exactly-once effects, and critical-path wall-time prediction.
Reviewed proof structure separating acyclicity, edge-specific readiness, physical equivalence, retry/effect safety, and performance evidence.
proof_review.notes: Graph structure supplies necessary dependency facts but cannot by itself prove capacity, data integrity, authorization, or end-to-end correctness.

evidence: Audited uses of acyclic, deterministic, equivalent, ready, committed, authoritative, atomic, idempotent, transactional, bounded, critical, reusable, and adaptive.
Confirmed the executable graph is labeled as a deterministic local structural model rather than an engine scheduler, resource simulation, or failure benchmark.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Engine-dependent behavior is attributed to declared contracts and verified plans rather than inferred from generic DAG terminology.

evidence: Reviewed graph construction/submission, queue, dispatch, useful CPU, serialization, spill, transfer, task duration, skew, cache lifetime, recovery, speculation, output, and critical-path evidence.
Confirmed no universal task size, cache threshold, fusion benefit, checkpoint interval, retry cost, graph limit, scheduler fairness, legal approval, or external-review claim is made.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production predictions require exact engine/code/plan, partitions, data distributions, resources, topology, contention, policies, and failure conditions.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed logical, physical, and runtime graphs; topology and cycle detection; edge availability; fusion, exchanges, and stages; tasks and attempts; work/span; fan-in/out; caching/checkpointing; retries/effects; adaptive rewrites; observability; replay; and governance as one execution model.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed plan and artifact identity, dependency closure, deterministic digests, stage/task mappings, resource evidence, skew, attempt isolation, atomic manifests, idempotency/outbox patterns, cache/checkpoint lifetime, cancellation, replay, sensitive lineage, policy enforcement, and named review. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from graph levels and topology through edge contracts, stages, work/span, state lifetime, failures, rewrites, and governance; ten examples and five complete answers cover traversal, proof, physical planning, publication safety, and regulated adaptive execution.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Spark, Beam, Flink, or Dask maintainer, distributed-systems researcher, graph-algorithms specialist, scheduler/performance engineer, security auditor, database transaction specialist, privacy/legal/records authority, affected-community reviewer, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
